errors.means: desk-web serves only browser_context and browser_command, and the name called is neither.
errors.fix: Call tools/list on desk-web and use one of the two names it lists.

doors.when: Before any page work, to get a contextId for a headless Edge or Chrome, or to end one and remove its temporary folder

errors.means: Opening mine, the operating system refused to let Desk read the person's browser profile, so no copy was opened.
errors.fix: Open a fresh browser instead; access to the profile is the operator's or an administrator's to grant.

errors.means: Opening mine, a required profile file could not be qualified (identity, single link or readable bytes), so no copy was opened.
errors.fix: Open a fresh browser instead; don't work around the refusal by controlling the person's own browser.

errors.means: Opening mine, the desk-web process runs with Node options, inspection or debug logging that could leak signed-in output.
errors.fix: Open a fresh browser, or have desk-web restarted without NODE_OPTIONS, DEBUG or an inspector.

errors.means: mine could not be opened safely, for example its browser driver didn't install or start; no other way of opening it was tried.
errors.fix: Open a fresh browser instead, or try mine again later.

errors.means: close named a context this server doesn't own, such as another live session's or an earlier Desk process's mine context.
errors.fix: Leave that context alone and open a new one; a server closes only its own contexts and fresh ones whose owner has gone.

errors.means: Closing a mine context, its cleanup couldn't be confirmed, so its private files were kept.
errors.fix: Call desk_doctor to see Desk's runtime state, and report it if the close fails again.

errors.means: A refusal with no code of its own: no Edge or Chrome installed, a fresh browser's driver didn't install, or a bad action, browser or contextId.
errors.fix: Read the message, which names the cause and the next step, such as installing a browser or passing open's contextId.

doors.when: After browser_context opens a context, for each page step: navigating, reading the accessibility tree, clicking, typing, taking pictures

errors.means: In mine, the page replaced or navigated away from the element since its ref was read.
errors.fix: Run ["snapshot"] again and act on a fresh ref; while a page loads, run ["wait","<text you expect>"] first.

errors.means: In mine, the ref isn't from one of the tab's recent reads, or its element has gone.
errors.fix: Take a new snapshot and use a ref from it.

errors.means: In mine, the arguments don't fit the command: the wrong number, an unknown flag or a wait out of range.
errors.fix: Check them against the commands the message lists and run the command again with corrected arguments.

errors.means: In mine, args[0] isn't one of the commands mine runs; the message lists them.
errors.fix: Use a listed command, or eval or run-code for anything the list doesn't cover.

errors.means: In mine, the eval or run-code script threw an error; the context stays open (a script still running at the time limit gets auth-timeout).
errors.fix: Fix the script from the error the message gives, and run it again.

errors.means: In mine, something on the page, such as a tooltip or menu, covers the control, and the action may have applied.
errors.fix: Press Escape or click what covers it, then act on a fresh ref from ["snapshot"].

errors.means: In mine, the control did not respond in time, and the action may have applied.
errors.fix: Take a new snapshot to see what happened, then act on a fresh ref; if the page keeps stalling, wait first.

errors.means: In mine, the context or its selected tab is closed, for example after an auth-timeout.
errors.fix: If the tab closed, run ["tab-list"] and select an open one; if the context closed, close it and open a new one.

errors.means: In mine, the command ran out of time, and Desk closed the context.
errors.fix: Close the old contextId, open a new context and start again from the page you were on, keeping waits under a minute.

errors.means: No open browser has that contextId, or in fresh the args fail its checks or the command failed or ran too long.
errors.fix: Read the message, which names the cause: open a context first, fix args, or run the command again.

errors.means: Desk's browser hit an unexpected problem with no safer message to give.
errors.fix: Call the tool again; if it repeats, call friction_add with the code.
